Blood, silence, and...regret. I still feel regret.


I watched the spark of life leave Nautus's eyes before rolling them and the others into the abyss below, where my new master waits. Defiance welled up inside, a few tears, one last gasp of air, but it's done.


I remember his fanged smile, before he returned me to my slumber the night before last, my bloodied daggers hidden where my waking self would not find them. Sintri, Marago, Odamos, they served Aria well... Now they'll serve him, too.


Soon, I'll join them in the ravaging nightmare, where I belong. My regret, my fear, my rage...they belong to him, now.

Stoic Alder,  
  
I want to thank you for inviting me to your battle's eve feast; it sounds like my kind of party! One of the hard truths I'm learning about leadership is that I can't just rush off whenever I want, which kind of frustrates every part of my being. Wolf yearns for the hunt, but I know I should heed Raven's wisdom; for now, my responsibilities in Cragstead require my attention.  
  
That said, make sure the commander enjoys several pints of honeywine in my place, and if you're planning on giving any prebattle speeches, it couldn't hurt to bend an ear their way for some pointers. I remember a particularly stirring call-to-arms they gave before our first bout with Kralkatorrik.  
  
Until our paths cross again, may your spears land true and the titans crack beneath your paws.  
  
—Braham Eirsson

A spirited discussion broke out in the mess hall today. We had taken to discussing the director, and on that subject, not a single objection or dissent could be found. Support for the director was so unanimous, in fact, that I feared we'd have yet another boring lunch.  
  
Then Snozzi chimed in about how she couldn't wait for the Inquest to be in control of the Tyrian Alliance. We all had a laugh at that absurdity, until that imbecile Prapp stated that *clearly* Director Vloxx intended to exterminate the non-asura, and thus would have no need of the alliance. Others jumped in quickly with equally foolish ideas, and I excused myself from the ensuing scuffle before Sebb could arrive and administer his own particular form of discipline.  
  
Suffice to say, it was a disconcerting experience. This expedition is supposed to consist of our best and brightest, and yet not one of them has the intelligence to see the utopia of technology that Vloxx is trying to build, with the Inquest guiding the way. But as long as they follow their misguided beliefs, they can still play their part. Many great successes have come from the careful deployment of useful fools.

Priory scholars have informed me of your triumph over the marionette that appeared near our monastery. The Durmand Priory owes you a debt once again, Commander—without your help, Scarlet Briar's monstrosity seemed impossible to confront.  Now it is beaten, and badly so—should it return, we have the means and knowledge to put a permanent end to it.

More importantly, we have pieced together data recovered from Scarlet's mechanical minions and made a remarkable discovery: the location of a concealed lair, hidden in the caves underneath the Priory itself.

A Priory dangerous artifacts investigation and containment team is being assembled as you read this, but in light of your seniority and field expertise, I have attached coordinates to the lair entrance, should you wish to make your own survey of the premises.

—Steward Gixx

Alder, Lahar, and I were sitting on the beach bones when a rumble sounded over the bay. Our hunting trip was halted—with a sound like that I half-expected to see the sky open up above us. But, nothing happened. Whatever it was, must've been further north.  
  
Storm rolled in pretty fast after, so we headed back to the den. Patient Willow told Lahar that they heard the same thing from all the way across the bay.

Naga found our camp two nights back. Gutted some of the crew and made off with most of our food stores before fleeing below.

Aria recruited a dozen of our most capable to follow. The chase below has been treacherous, but we were able to scavenge tools and salvage from the wrecked ships to get by. We have to; we'll starve otherwise.
